thread:
morgan: Heads-up — quick workshop in 30m to finalize the competitor hooks for next week's webinar. Goal: 1-pager per competitor bucket + 3 snappy rebut lines.
ana (Marketing): 👍 love it. Can we prioritize cloud AI platforms first? sales pick up those objections most.
rajesh (Product): Agree. Also want to add one benchmark callout: steady-state p99 latency + unit cost comparison for a 4K context. Keep the language non-technical for webinar slides.
taylor (Field): For infra vendors, SDRs keep hearing "we own our infra" — we should have a crisp economic riposte and a reliability angle. Something like: "Owning infra sounds good until tail latency and ops overhead hit — Redwood gives predictability without building it yourself."
morgan: Nice. Draft micro-rebut for cloud AI: 1) "Transparent unit economics vs opaque managed pricing" 2) "Deterministic fallbacks and SLA-backed capacity" 3) "Same API across hosted/dedicated/private" — shortlines only.
nana (Marketing): I'll run tone tests on those — want A/B variants for launch post and webinar CTA. Two variants: pragmatic (econ-first) and engineering (runtime-first).
rajesh (Product): For benchmark phrasing, avoid raw numbers in public claims — use ranges and customer-observed outcomes. e.g., "up to 3x lower per-token cost in high-throughput workloads" and link to deeper appendix.
taylor (Field): Inbound routing hooks matter: if prospect mentions "security/compliance" route to Private deck + enterprise CTA; "cost/latency" route to benchmark blog + demo signup. Can we make a routing template?
morgan: @rajesh can you own the routing template? simple YAML snippet for SDRs they can copy into Intercom.
rajesh (Product): Yep. I'll drop a starter template in #sales-assets after the workshop. Example snippet to share:
```
route_criteria:
  - intent: "security"
    destination: "private-deck"
  - intent: "latency"
    destination: "benchmark-blog"
```

morgan: Perfect. Ana — can you run the tone tests and draft the two hero lines for the webinar landing page? Target completion by EOD today.
nana (Marketing): On it. I'll post options in this thread and ping @taylor for field realism checks.
dev-bot: Reminder: webinar slides repo updated: git push to `webinar/2026-q2` may require rebase.
taylor (Field): Quick field check — for infra vendors, include one sentence: "Why a unified runtime beats stitching multiple vendor APIs (less vendor lock, fewer integrations)." Short and punchy.
rajesh (Product): Adding that to the competitor bucket doc.
morgan: Action items recap: 1) @ana: tone tests + 2 hero lines (EOD). 2) @rajesh: routing YAML + competitor bucket updates (after workshop). 3) @taylor: one-sentence vendor rebut + field examples. We'll review 16:30 PT. See you in 30. :rocket:
